steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Quality control (QC) inspects the finished product to detect defects - it's reactive and occurs after production. Defective items are rejected or reworked.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Quality assurance (QA) builds quality into every stage of the production process - it's proactive and aims to prevent defects before they occur.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Total quality management (TQM) involves every employee in continuous quality improvement: zero defects culture, employee empowerment, and customer focus throughout the organisation.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: ISO 9001 is an international quality standard: businesses must document processes, demonstrate consistent quality, and pass regular audits. Certification builds customer trust.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Remember: quality control is REACTIVE (after), quality assurance is PROACTIVE (during). This distinction is a common exam question. Link quality to cost: it's cheaper to prevent defects than to fix them - the 'cost of quality' includes both prevention costs and failure costs. TQM is a CULTURE, not just a system - it requires commitment from top management and involvement from every employee.
